newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Jan exports show strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Jan exports show strong growth.

text.p: Philippine merchandise exports in January jumped 18.8 percent to $1.688 billion from $1.420 billion in the year earlier, boosted by robust electronics sales, the National Statistics Office (NSO) reported on Tuesday.
On a month-on-month basis, exports fell by 10.4 percent from $1.883 billion in December.
Economists said the January trend indicated the country was likely to meet its export growth target this year of over 20 percent to $25 billion.
In 1996, exports grew by 17.7 percent to $20.531 billion compared with $17.447 billion in 1995.
Joel Mendoza, vice-president for research of Banco Santander in Manila, described January's increase as "very strong".

"The very good export performance reflects the improvement in world trade conditions," Ofelia Templo, assistant director-general of the government's National Economic Development Authority, told Reuters.
Analysts said export growth in January was high at a time when exports usually ease off after the brisk sales in the last quarter of every year.
Exports could have been stronger if not for the slowdown in the garments sector, which had been outpriced by countries with cheaper labour, analysts said.
The government said exports of electronics and components posted year-on-year growth of 30.9 percent to $732.86 million in January, while garment exports fell 26.96 percent to $144.29 million.
Electronic exports comprised 43.4 percent of the country's overseas sales in January, while garments accounted for 8.5 percent.
Despite the contraction in garment sales, Santander's Mendoza believes export growth this year will be higher.
"There's momentum in the electronics sector. And a lot electronic-related companies will set up shop here," he said.
Japan's TDK Corp has announced plans to invest 18.309 billion pesos (US$696 million) over the next five years to set up a production plant for magnetic heads and components in the Philippines.
Japan's Toshiba Corp has said it will spend an additional six billion yen ($49.5 million) until the year 2000 on its Philippine unit to expand product lines.
On the garments sector, analysts said productivity will have to be improved to fight competition from other countries.
Carina Legaspi, an economist at Union Bank of the Philippines, said the country would have to diversify its product lines to sustain export growth. ($1 = 26.3 pesos)
